newsitem.title: TAIWAN: GE turns up heat in Taiwan nuclear plant showdown.
newsitem.headline: GE turns up heat in Taiwan nuclear plant showdown.

text.p: General Electric Co. turned up the heat in a political showdown over Taiwan's fourth nuclear power station, indicating it would seek compensation if construction were delayed beyond Wednesday.
GE served notice on state utility Taiwan Power Co. that it would not extend a midnight deadline for starting work on the stalled project, Taipower officials said.
"This means GE would be able to seek compensation if parliament does not agree to support the project by midnight tonight," Lin said.

Despite GE's deadline, the fate of the US$4.1 billion power plant -- and GE's US$1.8 billion contract to supply its twin reactors and generators -- remained undecided pending a final vote in parliament scheduled for Friday.
GE officials in Taipei declined to comment on the notice.
